submission.natural_language_explanation: The positive pole fires at the seam where one structural unit of a formatted text closes and the next opens. It is strong (about 1.0-1.7) on the closing delimiter of a multi-line block that sits at a line boundary - '}' '};' or '});' ending a code block, '*/' ending a block comment, '$$' or '$' ending display math, '>' ending a multi-line tag, '].' or ']]' ending a bracketed reference list (strength rises with the number of lines closed, and '});', '*/', '$$' and '].' fire even on short blocks) - and moderate (about 0.55-1.0) on the first word of a new paragraph when that word opens an additive or contrastive connective ('However', 'In addition', 'Moreover', 'On the other hand', 'By contrast', 'Meanwhile', 'Also', 'Next', 'The second'); those same characters used inside a single sentence (an inline '{ ... }', '[[link]]', '$x$', a short '( ... )', a one-line '/* ... */') and running prose with neither a block-closing delimiter nor a paragraph-initial connective stay at or below the firing line, with their peak set only by incidental sentence-initial words (typically 0.3-0.5).
